CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

zugojson formats, minifies and validates JSON text with a parser and printer written in Goose (https://github.com/aardappel/goose) and compiled ahead of time to C. It is a demonstration that a Goose library can be bundled in an R package, not a jsonlite competitor. It has no hard runtime dependencies. It does not convert JSON to R objects yet.

.agents/design.md and .agents/roadmap.md are still the pkg-init stubs. Until they are written, this file is the reference.

Current state

Verified 2026-10-25 on Linux, R 4.6.1:

  • json_format(), json_minify() and json_valid() work, with classed conditions for parse, input and runtime errors.
  • R CMD check --as-cran is clean apart from the new-submission NOTE.
  • The test suite passes, including jsonlite as an oracle.
  • macOS should work, because it uses the same POSIX code, but it has not been run. Windows is not written: goose_r_runtime.c stops the build with an #error, and DESCRIPTION says OS_type: unix.
  • About twice as slow as jsonlite; the README has the numbers.
  • Not built: parsing to R lists, path queries, and the Windows runtime.

Commands

Run from the package root.

Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'                # roxygen -> NAMESPACE, man/
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'                    # full testthat suite
Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'                   # R CMD check
tools/regenerate.sh <goose-checkout>             # rewrite generated C
tools/regenerate.sh --verify <goose-checkout>    # check it is current
tools/check-symbols.sh <path>/zugojson.so        # forbidden symbols

The Goose checkout must be at the commit in tools/goose/PIN and built with cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build.

devtools::load_all() compiles at -O0. Benchmark an installed build.

Architecture

tools/goose/zugojson.goose   the parser and printer, in Goose (the source)
tools/regenerate.sh          Goose -> the four generated files in src/
src/zugojson_goose.{c,h}     generated: the program, with no main
src/goose_version.h          generated: the runtime interface hash
src/goose_vendor.c           generated: byte search and number formatting,
                             verbatim from Goose's runtime_impl.h
src/goose_r_runtime.{c,h}    the replacement Goose runtime for R
src/zugojson_number.c        strtod for the parser, through an extern fn
src/zugojson_r.c             the .Call entry points
R/json.R                     the R API and the condition constructors

The R-to-Goose boundary is goose_r_run(). Every call into generated code goes through it, including goose_init() in R_init_zugojson(). It saves each data stack’s top and installs the guard-page fault handler. A Goose failure then jumps back to it, the tops are rewound and the handlers restored, and it returns the message. The entry point raises the R condition only after that.

Exports return bytes plus a length. A syntax error comes back as text starting with !, which rendered JSON never does. The .Call functions return c(kind, text), and unwrap() in R turns a non-empty kind into a condition.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • No R API inside goose_r_run(). A body function or anything Goose calls, such as zugojson_strtod, must not allocate R objects or raise R errors. An R longjmp would skip the stack rewind and leave Goose’s SIGSEGV handler in place of R’s.
  • Every export clears its globals first. After a failure the data stack tops are rewound but Goose globals are not. An export that relies on what a previous call left in pool or out reads half-built state.
  • Never edit generated files. CI rebuilds Goose at the pin and fails if src/zugojson_goose.c, its header, goose_version.h or goose_vendor.c differ from what tools/regenerate.sh writes.
  • Generated code has no capacity checks. Goose relies on a PROT_NONE guard gap after each data stack. gs_reserve_region() must keep that gap and the fault handler must keep turning a hit into a runtime error, or an overflow becomes a crash.
  • The nesting limit protects the C stack. Rendering and parsing recurse. Without the 512 limit in parse_value, deep input overflows the native stack, which no handler here catches.
  • Bumping the Goose pin can change the runtime interface. The version hash in goose_version.h makes a mismatch a link error. Read the diff of Goose’s runtime.h too: a new GS_API function the generated C references needs an implementation in goose_r_runtime.c or a new range in goose_vendor.c. Link at -O0, because -O2 hides references from unused inline helpers.
  • The __int128 patch. tools/regenerate.sh wraps the 128-bit type in __extension__, because -pedantic calls it “ISO C”, which R CMD check counts as significant. The script fails if the anchor is not found exactly once.
  • The symbol names gs_* are Goose’s. They cannot take the package prefix, because the generated C calls them by those names.

Testing conventions

  • Every test builds its own inputs inside test_that().
  • Assert on condition classes, never message text.
  • jsonlite is the oracle in test-jsonlite.R, skipped when it is missing. It checks that formatting does not change what a document means.
  • test-runtime.R drives the runtime’s error path through zugojson_index_probe, a Goose export that fails a bounds check on demand. A data stack overflow is not tested in the suite, because it needs stacks shrunk at compile time. It was tested by hand with -DGS_STACK_RESERVE='(1ull<<20)' in PKG_CPPFLAGS.

Definition of done

devtools::document() and devtools::check() clean, meaning 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 notes, except “New submission” before the first release. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) green. tools/regenerate.sh --verify passes. A user-facing change also needs a test, roxygen documentation and a NEWS.md entry.

Editing rules

  • Change the JSON code in tools/goose/zugojson.goose, then run tools/regenerate.sh, and commit both together.
  • roxygen comments are the source. Never edit man/ or NAMESPACE by hand.
  • Keep prose simple and short. One idea per sentence.
  • Use lower_snake_case, and prefix first-party native symbols with zugojson_.

Vendored native code

Goose, Apache-2.0, Wouter van Oortmerssen. The pinned commit is in tools/goose/PIN, and tools/goose/PROVENANCE records the checksums of the generated files. inst/licenses/goose-LICENSE is upstream’s licence, and inst/COPYRIGHTS lists which files it covers.

The stock runtime, src/runtime/runtime_impl.h upstream, is not vendored. Only goose_vendor.c’s verbatim ranges come from it. CRAN’s compiled-code check applies to everything: tools/check-symbols.sh fails on exit, _exit, _Exit, abort, stdout, stderr, the printf family and the system RNG, and goose.yaml runs it on Linux and macOS.

Upstream defects found

  • Goose’s parse_flt in stdlib/std.goose can be one ulp off for long mantissas and large exponents, as its own comment says. 1e300 reads back as 1.0000000000000002e+300. zugojson uses strtod instead.
  • The stock runtime has no way for an embedding host to take over aborts and printing. A hook for that would remove most of goose_r_runtime.c.

Neither has been reported upstream yet.

Commits and pull requests

Short, imperative, sentence-case commit subjects. Never commit or push to the default branch. Work on a branch and open a pull request. A change to the pin, the runtime or tools/regenerate.sh must say so in the pull request.
